entries.title: Hex Survival Gamemode Development Update
entries.summary: Major Survival gamemode development pass: real 1v1 encounters, DBC/JRM scaling, scoring, rewards, KO handling, transformations, safe spawning, and GUI optimization.
details: PASS 1 — Built the authoritative Survival state engine with IDLE, LOBBY, PRE_FIGHT, FIGHTING, ROUND_COMPLETE, INTERMISSION, and terminal states. Added 64-bit run/player counters and a one-active-opponent encounter model.

PASS 2.x — Added the fighting-game presentation layer with READY, CLEAR, FAILED, and RESULTS screens, full-body portrait support, animated score/body readouts, Continue/Close actions, and GUI ambient audio.

PASS 3 — Replaced fake/debug telemetry with a real encounter vertical slice: saved CustomNPC clone spawning, actual opponent death detection, server-controlled Continue progression, DBC Body/Ki/Stamina reads, combo telemetry, and separate run/fight timers.

PASS 3.1 — Fixed CustomNPC+/DBC/HUD stability by using the exact CustomNPC+ spawnClone route, validating clones before PRE_FIGHT, using safer JRMCore resource reads, and keeping the active-run HUD visible across states.

PASS 4 — Added END RUN cash-out and score-to-reward conversion. Initial rewards included TP and vanilla EXP with D/C/B/A/S/Z rank previews, one-time reward finalization, and a persistent reward queue.

PASS 4.1 — Reworked CLEAR/RESULTS rows into a clipped scrollable viewport while keeping END RUN and CONTINUE fixed. Added mouse-wheel, arrow-key, and Page Up/Page Down scrolling. This renderer was intentionally structured for future generic reward screens.
PASS 4.1.1 — Fixed the Minecraft 1.7.10 GuiScreen.handleMouseInput override by removing the invalid IOException declaration.

PASS 4.2 — Hardened JRM/world-load behavior. Survival stopped creating/reconnecting JRM data during reads, reduced reward polling, removed per-hit HUD packet spam, and changed missing/unloaded opponents so they no longer count as defeated.

PASS 5A — Added autonomous player-relative NPC scaling. Survival snapshots the player's DBC stats at spawn and scales the spawned CustomNPC's HP, melee, and regen automatically. The NPC script remains responsible for its character-specific transformations, animations, aura, dialogue, and phases.
SCALING BASELINE — Reused the established six-stat DBC level formula based on STR, DEX, CON, WIL, MND, and SPI, while keeping saved-clone HP/melee useful as template/base values.
PASS 5A.1 — Attempted death/respawn cleanup improvements with stronger tagged-opponent removal and delayed results around the vanilla/DBC death lifecycle.

PASS 5A.2 — Rebalanced autonomous scaling against JRMCore's Training Shadow Dummy behavior. Added hybrid Shadow/legacy scaling, anti-one-shot melee caps, and corrected Damage Dealt telemetry by measuring real opponent HP loss instead of trusting LivingHurtEvent damage values that DBC/NPCDBC may rewrite.
PASS 5A.2.1 — Packaging/build fix: included the updated SurvivalRun and SurvivalCustomNpcSpawner companion methods required by the newer controller.

PASS 5A.3 — Added increasing endless-round difficulty. Later rounds gain HP, melee pressure, and regen multipliers, with HP/regen increasing more aggressively than offense. Also tested a temporary delayed-respawn guard after discovering quick respawn could race DBC/JRMCore synchronization.

DEATH TEST FINDING — Waiting several seconds before pressing vanilla Respawn avoided the repeated-death issue, confirming a DBC/JRMCore quick-respawn synchronization race rather than ordinary Survival lag.

PASS 5A.4 — Replaced real player death with a Survival KO system. When DBC Body reaches 0 or below, Survival restores the player to 1 DBC Body and 1 vanilla HP, removes the opponent, ends the run, finalizes rewards, and shows RESULTS without entering the vanilla/DBC death-respawn lifecycle.
PASS 5A.4.1 — Packaging/build fix: included the roundHealthScale, roundDamageScale, and roundRegenScale snapshot fields and matching scaling-engine changes.

ROUND DIFFICULTY — Round 1 starts at the player's normal relative baseline. Subsequent rounds progressively increase HP, damage pressure, and regen while remaining behind the DBC Body anti-one-shot safeguards. Deeper rounds also contribute additional score.

PASS 5B — Added immutable fight snapshots and a dedicated SurvivalScoreCalculator. CLEAR now shows a deterministic score breakdown including base opponent value, challenge, effective damage, Body remaining, combo, quick-finish speed, depth, transformations, boss status, and perfect-round bonuses.
CHALLENGE SCORING — Opponent difficulty is compared against the player's effective Survival scaling so weaker opponents award less and increasingly difficult rounds award more.

TRANSFORMATION TELEMETRY — Survival records opponent transformations reported by the NPC script and also watches conservative DBC player-form state changes during the fight. The NPC script still owns when and how transformations occur.

NPC TRANSFORMATION TEST — SSJ2 and SSJ3 are currently tester forms. The transformation script uses display.transform(), enables the NPCDBC aura during/after the transformation, and reports the form change back to Survival.
PASS 5B.1 — Forced NPCDBC DBC Skin on for Survival fighters and reasserted DBC Skin/aura during the tester transformations.

SAFE SPAWNING — Added collision/block checks around candidate spawn positions so fighters search for a safe loaded location instead of spawning inside walls. Survival fails cleanly if no valid nearby position exists and does not intentionally force chunk generation.

LEVEL SCORE BONUS — Added a soft-capped player-level contribution to score so higher-level DBC players have greater reward potential without letting ~15,000+ level characters multiply rewards uncontrollably. Approximate level bonus is ~2.6% at Lv1000, ~5.8% at Lv5000, ~8.2% at Lv10000, and ~10% at Lv15000, with only a small diminishing logarithmic tail above that.
SCORE TUNING — Added a small +4% overall Survival score tuning bump on top of the level-aware score system.
HAKI REWARDS — Added Survival Haki EXP. Reward EXP goes to unlocked Haki mastery tracks, or Armament awakening progression when no Haki track is currently unlocked.
SWORD REWARDS — Added shared Sword Style / Haki-sword EXP as a Survival reward rather than creating a separate incompatible sword EXP bank.

REWARD CURVES — Haki EXP uses approximately sqrt(totalScore) * 0.85 * rank factor with a 5000 cap. Sword Style EXP uses approximately sqrt(totalScore) * 1.15 * rank factor with a 7500 cap. Rank factors are D 0.8, C 0.9, B 1.0, A 1.1, S 1.25, and Z 1.4.
RESULT REWARDS — CLEAR/RESULTS can now display TP, vanilla EXP, Haki EXP, and Sword Style EXP alongside rank and score information.

GUI FPS PASS — Optimized dense CLEAR/RESULTS rendering after repeated rounds began affecting FPS. Only visible scroll rows are sent through the renderer, dense stat rows use static gradients, decorative motion is reduced on large score screens, and stale GUI ambient sounds are stopped more aggressively between repeated screens.

CURRENT DESIGN — CustomNPCs remains the primary fighter-authoring route because scripts can control forms, phases, attacks, dialogue, animations, and gimmicks. The Survival engine is being kept generic enough to later mix CustomNPC/NPCDBC fighters with native DBC and Ninjin entities through adapter-style opponent handling.

FUTURE DIRECTION — Continue expanding real combat telemetry, special-skill tracking, fighter registries/random encounter selection, native DBC/Ninjin opponent adapters, boss/depth progression, money/item reward pools, and reuse of the Survival scroll/result GUI as a general-purpose reward screen.

entries.title: Major Rendering & FPS Improvements
entries.summary: Major FPS improvements for HexFont, rarity-heavy inventories, chests, and dropped item effects.
details: Greatly improved FPS when opening chests and inventories containing large amounts of rarity and HexColorText-enabled items.
Rarity overlays now reuse cached rarity, evolved tier, pseudo-black, chaos tier, and visual information instead of repeatedly scanning item lore and NBT every render frame.
Added faster HexFont rendering paths for ordinary GUI text such as item stack counts so non-HyperText text can bypass unnecessary compatibility and styled-text processing.
Reduced repeated NBT serialization, lore parsing, regex checks, and other expensive per-frame item calculations.
Dropped-item rarity beams now cache nearby item scans rather than searching for EntityItems every rendered frame.
Item beams now reuse cached rarity and evolved item data instead of independently rebuilding visual state.
Added adaptive detail scaling to decorative rarity gloss, item beam geometry, chaos sparks, rings, halos, and flare effects when client FPS begins to fall.
Expanded general HexFont performance handling while preserving full gradients, glow, outlines, animated text, and other HyperText effects whenever performance allows.
Overall rendering is now considerably more stable during normal gameplay, item-heavy inventories, large chests, and areas containing many custom rarity drops.

entries.title: Equipment Enhancement, Modern Gem Effects and HexSocket Visual Refresh
entries.summary: Expanded equipment enhancement to support customized gear while improving rolled stats, modernizing legacy gem particles, refreshing HexSocket visuals and adding enhancement-tier crafting colors.
details: Equipment enhancement recipes now match the underlying registered item rather than requiring identical rarity, rolled stats, sockets, evolution data, custom lore or other custom NBT.

Three copies of the same registered weapon, armor piece or accessory can now be used together regardless of rarity or other customization, while all three must still share the same current enhancement level.

The center crafting-grid item is preferred as the preserved main item. Its rarity, rolled attributes, sockets, evolution state, custom name, lore, enchantments, durability and other supported item data carry into the enhancement result while the two donor copies are consumed.
Successful enhancement now strengthens eligible rolled combat stats. Weapons gain 2.5% rolled-stat improvement per + level, armor gains 2.0% per level and accessories gain 1.5% per level.

Enhancement stat growth uses a separately tracked enhancement layer so changing + levels does not repeatedly compound already-enhanced values, while negative rolls improve toward zero instead of becoming worse.

Reworked the Rainbow / Swirly gem family with modern individually colored rainbow particles, smooth orbit and spiral motion, prismatic ribbons and white, cyan, magenta and gold accent sparkles while substantially reducing legacy vanilla particle spam.
Reworked the Fire gem with cleaner modern flame wisps, rising embers and red, orange, amber and gold accents across its aura, impacts, damage-over-time effects and larger bursts.
Refreshed the HexSocket decorative gem display using newer existing artwork including Evolved Rainbow, Celestial Core, Crystalline Ocean, Glitch Prism, Astral Prism and Evolved Inferno visuals.

The crafting-table enhancement HUD now changes visual theme with the target + level: silver and ice for +1 through +4, blue and cyan for +5 through +8, violet and magenta for +9 through +11, gold for +12 through +13, crimson and gold for +14, and the highest rainbow treatment for +15.
Updated enhancement descriptions to make it clear that the recipe requires three copies of the same underlying item while rarity and other custom item data are allowed to differ.

entries.title: JRMC Tech Bridge, Progressive Dragon Wishes and Native Charge Scaling
entries.bannerTitle: JRMC TECH / DRAGON WISHES / CUSTOM ATTACKS
entries.summary: Black Coffin, Grapple and Dragon Fist were added to a progressive Dragon Ball wish system and integrated with JRMCore's custom technique controls, charge bar and resource handling.
details: Added Black Coffin, Grapple and Dragon Fist as progressive Dragon Ball wish families.
Repeated wishes upgrade the currently owned family version instead of granting a duplicate skill.
Black Coffin progresses through Normal, Full Incantation and Third Form.
Grapple progresses through Hold, Throw and Slam.
Dragon Fist progresses through Normal, Rush, Loop and Blast.
Trying to wish for a fully completed family is rejected without consuming the player's wish.
A wish is also rejected safely when every available JRMC custom technique slot is occupied.
Custom Hex techniques are restricted to jrmcTech1 through jrmcTech4.
JRMC special slots 5 through 8 are never written, replaced or used by the Hex technique bridge.
New skill families automatically use the next genuinely empty custom technique slot.
Upgrading a family replaces the previous version in the same JRMC slot.
Black Coffin and Dragon Fist can be selected through the JRMC technique interface and activated with Second Function plus Energy Release or Right Click.
The native JRMC charge bar now controls the released percentage of Black Coffin and Dragon Fist.
The attacks use their original Hex damage and Ki formulas instead of the small placeholder Blast or Large Blast values.
Damage and Ki cost scale together with the player's JRMC release level and final charge percentage.
Dragon Fist now consumes its intended thousands of Ki at full charge instead of the generic JRMC cost of only a few points.
Failed targeting, cooldown, spawning or casting checks do not consume Ki or Body.
Reserved Ki and Body are restored when an attack cannot complete.
Added the logical Strike technique category for grapples, dashes and physical attacks.
Added the logical Ultimate technique category for cinematic attacks, finishers and large-area techniques.
Strike and Ultimate use safe existing JRMCore carrier types internally to avoid modifying JRMCore's fixed technique arrays.
The JRMC technique preview now displays the same Hex-calculated damage and Ki cost used by the server cast.
Black Coffin upgrades now resolve the active tier from authoritative progression NBT, preventing stale JRMC slot data from casting the wrong version.
Full Incantation now performs its chant sequence while the JRMC charge input is held.
Releasing the charge completes the active Black Coffin incantation instead of beginning a separate instant cast.
Black Coffin Normal, Full Incantation and Third Form received increased configurable damage scaling.
Full Incantation and Third Form attack jobs now remain alive for their complete cinematic timelines and correctly damage their selected target.
Black Coffin and Dragon Fist slot builds periodically refresh to repair temporary missing or stale client technique entries.
Removing or replacing the final equipped technique for a wish family resets that family's progression NBT.
Moving the same family technique between custom slots 1 through 4 does not reset its progression.
All custom slot handling remains isolated from JRMC special slots to prevent player technique-data corruption.

entries.title: Modern Swimming, Native Skill Animations, Haki Damage and Coating Overhaul
entries.bannerTitle: MODERN MOVEMENT / HAKI VISUALS / COMBAT POLISH
entries.summary: This development pass modernized swimming and sword combat while correcting Haki damage and expanding Haki coating visuals. New systems use native DBC/JBRA model hooks, optimized modern particles, multiplayer-synchronized animation phases and item-local coating textures. Player coatings now inherit JRMCore Constitution scaling and remain correctly attached to customized JBRA models.
details: MASTERED HAKI FINISHERS
Added a timed HUD window to supported mastered sword skills.
Finishers activate by releasing and pressing right-click again inside the timing window.
Final-slash damage scales primarily from STR with separate timing and mastery multipliers.
Perfect inputs trigger stronger impact frames and increased damage.
Finishers teleport the player to a collision-safe position beside the nearest valid target.
Added server-side mastery, held-item, slot, timing and packet validation.
MODERN SWIMMING BACKPORT
Added automatic treading, normal swimming, sprint swimming and low-space crawling states.
Added pitch-based diving and rising with jump and sneak vertical controls.
Added compact swimming and crawling dimensions with safe standing restoration.
Added water-exit assistance and multiplayer swimming-state synchronization.
Replaced the failed CustomNPC+ animation route with native DBC and JBRA model-animation hooks.
Added smooth modern-style 26-tick swimming strokes with blended body rotation.
Removed land-movement stutter, unnecessary idle packets and repeated hitbox updates.
MODERN WATER PARTICLES
Added splash, bubble-pop and wake effects when entering or leaving water.
Added surface bubbles, underwater motes, sprint wakes and dolphin-style trails.
Added rising bubble-column and downward-current effects.
Added modern and legacy particle-name translation support.
Reused the existing 26.2 particle assets without adding duplicate textures.
NATIVE SWORD ANIMATIONS
Added smooth DBC and JBRA-native charge, cast and impact animations.
Added unique animation styles for upward cuts, thrusts, heavy overhead attacks and multi-slashes.
Added stronger follow-through animations for mastered finishers.
Animation phases synchronize to nearby players without transmitting limb rotations every frame.
Added animation support for the main Haki sword-skill families and their Asura variants.
HAKI DAMAGE CORRECTION
Moved complete Haki scaling into the original authoritative damage event.
Haki levels now change the primary displayed damage number instead of creating a secondary correction hit.
Removed duplicate normal-hit jrmcDam corrections.
Added silent DBC Body reconciliation when a target under-applies the requested damage.
Standardized requested Haki damage across vanilla mobs, CustomNPCs, NPCDBC and DBC entities.
Fixed custom weapons consuming Ki twice for the same coated hit.
HAKI WEAPON COATING
Added separate Armament, Ryuo and Conqueror coating appearances.
Added mode-specific inventory textures for Blackblaze Katana, Phoenix Nodachi, Spiral Guard Katana, Cursed Blade and Energy Scythe stages.
Added mode-specific held-model textures for supported custom weapons.
Removed the inaccurate floating world-space blade overlay.
Weapon coating now remains attached to the actual item model during normal movement and skill animations.
HAKI PLAYER COATING
Added progression-based hand and forearm coating directly to the active JRMCore and JBRA arm geometry.
Armament begins around the weapon hand while higher Haki levels extend farther along both forearms.
Added a lowered gradual fade between coated and uncoated areas.
Added animated flowing glow ribbons and traveling energy rings around coated arms.
Added Ryuo pressure accents and Conqueror lightning cracks around the arms and player silhouette.
Coating and glow effects now inherit JRMCore Constitution-based body scaling.
Arm effects remain aligned with enlarged players, JBRA proportions, arm rotations and active animations.
Prevented coating hooks from affecting player legs or detached torso geometry.
Prevented the vanilla Minecraft skin from rendering over or leaking through customized JBRA skins.
Normal skin rendering remains unchanged while Haki is inactive.
PERFORMANCE AND COMPATIBILITY
Added distance limits, per-tick particle caps and cached Haki render state.
Consolidated coated-hit effects into compact packets expanded on the client.
Removed repeated animation creation, unnecessary render passes and redundant particle assets.
Kept normal land movement and non-Haki rendering on fast zero-work paths.
Kept the flowing glow on a separate additive pass without replacing the depth-correct Haki coating.
Verified native animation and coating hooks against JRMCore 1.3.51 and JBRA Client 1.6.52.
Trimmed about 5MB in file size(Removed unused textures).

entries.title: Modern Movement, Native Combat Animations and Haki Visuals
entries.summary: Modern swimming, server-synced native animations, corrected Haki damage, and expanded Haki coating visuals were added in this development pass.
details: Added mastered Haki finisher windows with right-click timing, impact frames, STR scaling, and collision-safe target blink attacks.
Corrected Haki level scaling so the full coated hit is applied and displayed as the primary damage number across vanilla, DBC, NPCDBC, and CustomNPC targets.
Backported modern treading, swimming, sprint swimming, crawling, dive/rise controls, compact dimensions, and optimized 26.2 water particles.
Added smooth native DBC/JBRA charge, cast, impact, and follow-through animations for the main Haki sword techniques.
Added server-authoritative grapple hold, held-target, throw, Xenoverse-style Sledgehammer slam-down, Dragon Fist, and Black Coffin animation phases visible to nearby players.
Added Armament, Ryuo, and Conqueror coating variants for custom weapons plus compact mode-aware hit presets through the modern particle pipeline.
Added progression-based hand and forearm coating with Ryuo flow accents and Conqueror lightning while preserving both vanilla skins and JBRA character customization.
Added separate vanilla and enlarged-JBRA coating calibration so each player renderer keeps the intended hand-to-forearm fade.
Optimized animation, particle, packet, NBT, and render paths with cached state, distance limits, phase-only synchronization, and zero-work inactive paths.

entries.title: HexFont Renderer Performance Overhaul (Attempt)
entries.summary: HexFont received a multi-phase performance overhaul focused on improving frame stability when many animated HyperText strings are visible. Parser patterns are now reused, parsed operation trees and text measurements are globally cached, animated render plans are shared per frame, and compatible gradient, rainbow, wave, outline, and glow passes are batched through Tessellator. CustomNPC nameplates, scripted GUIs, overlays, and native NPC list screens now use dedicated fast paths that avoid repeated stack scans, parsing, width checks, and character-by-character truncation. Phase 7 also introduces persistent animated glyph-command templates so static glyph positions and font UV data can be reused while animation colors and offsets continue updating normally. Vanilla text, HexHelp interactions, CustomNPC quest alerts, JRMCore, NPCDBC, chat, dialogs, and unsupported render combinations retain their guarded fallback behavior.

entries.title: Complete Chat Wrapping + Seamless HexHub Gradients
entries.summary: HyperText wrapping now preserves complete styles for NPC and player chat, while HexHub gradients loop without dark hard seams.
details: NPC say messages now wrap as complete HyperText lines, preserving gradient, outline, shadow, glow, bold, and other active wrappers on continuation lines.
Player HyperText messages now use the same complete-line wrapping setup while ordinary unformatted player chat remains on its normal wrapping path.
HexHub custom tag gradients no longer jump directly from the final color back to the first color while scrolling.
Open-ended palettes now travel forward and backward through the supplied colors, removing the dark or black-looking hard seam without inventing extra colors.
Tag text and its matching gradient pill background use the same seamless palette behavior.

entries.title: Nested HexFont Style Rendering Fix
entries.summary: Nested glow, outline, gradient, and shake tags now render one styled text fill instead of leaving a duplicate vanilla text layer behind.
details: Fixed nested <glow>, <outline>, <grad>, and <shake> combinations drawing the original vanilla text behind the styled result.
Glow now preserves the nested gradient or animated fill unless an explicit glow text color is supplied.
The fix covers examples such as Super Saiyan Full Power and Super Saiyan 2 without removing the existing HexFont bypasses or GUI guards.
Existing single-style rendering and explicit fill/color behavior remain unchanged.

entries.title: Haki Skill EXP, Bleed, Counter and NPC Pound Phoenix Update
entries.summary: Fixed EXP crediting for Pound Phoenix, Multi Slash and Phoenix Rend, including transformed skill variants. Pound Phoenix now requires a sufficiently strong target to award EXP. Added protection against Totem passive bonuses stacking, upgraded Tiger Hunt with a forward strike and visual return dash, expanded bleed support to weapon Haki skills after Tier 1, added tier-scaled multi-hit dashes to Lion's Requiem counters, and exposed Pound Phoenix for CustomNPCs scripting.

entries.title: Tiered Bleeds + Orb Upgrade Levels
entries.summary: Phoenix Rend, Tiger Hunt, and successful Lion counters can now leave capped tier-scaled bleeds, while rolled Hex orbs can be combined in threes for risky +1 through +5 upgrades that strengthen their existing stats.
entries.actionSubtitle: Haki bleed effects and three-orb upgrades
details: Phoenix Rend and Tiger Hunt now apply a bleed whenever their direct Haki damage successfully lands.
Lion's Requiem applies its bleed only when the Lion Counter path successfully damages the target.
Bleed damage scales at 1.5% of the triggering hit per skill tier and lasts longer at higher tiers.
The bleed pulses once per second, refreshes or strengthens instead of stacking without limit, and is capped at 30% total damage from the triggering hit.
Each successful bleed pulse creates a dark-red modern trail burst and critical-hit particles around the affected entity.
Three rolled orbs of the exact same kind, subtype, and current + level can now be placed anywhere in a 3x3 crafting table for an upgrade attempt.
Upgrade progression is capped at +5 and the successful level is added directly to the orb's displayed name.
Success chances are 75% for +1, 65% for +2, 55% for +3, 45% for +4, and 35% for +5.
A successful attempt returns one upgraded orb. A failed attempt consumes two orbs and returns one unchanged orb.
The strongest roll among the three matching inputs is used as the result base before the upgrade is resolved.
Every successful + level improves flat rolls by roughly 5% with at least +1 gained, while percentage rolls gain +1 percentage point per level.
Negative rolls move slightly toward zero when upgraded, and + levels are preserved through supported orb rerolls.
Upgraded orbs are blocked from the older Enhanced and Evolved recipes so their + level cannot be erased accidentally.

entries.title: Cleaner Live HyperText Editing in Chat
entries.summary: HyperText tags are now easier to write and edit directly inside the Minecraft chat box.
changes: Unfinished HyperText tags now remain visible while they are being typed.
Completed opening tags disappear after the closing > is entered.
Completed closing tags also disappear once fully written.
Message text continues displaying with the active HyperText formatting.
Moving the cursor into a completed tag reveals the section being edited.
Removed the duplicate HyperText preview that could overlap the normal chat input.

entries.summary: <grad #FFD86B #FFFFFF #FF9A3D scroll=0.08>The custom Totem of Undying now has upgraded activation effects, preservation procs, working DBC stat bonuses, animated textures, and a visible buff timer.</grad>
details: <glow #FFB347><grad #FFD86B #FFFFFF #FF9A3D scroll=0.09 styles=l>Reworked the custom Totem of Undying activation.</grad></glow> It now preserves the expected death-prevention behavior while playing synchronized activation sounds, particles, and client animation effects.

entries.title: Haki Balance Configs + Server Charge Support + Haki Edge
entries.summary: HexHaki received a major combat polish pass with cleaner Conqueror unlocks, safer charged-skill validation for multiplayer servers, configurable sword technique balance, shorter config GUI names with hover explanations, and a new Haki Edge custom enchantment that boosts sword skill and active Haki damage.
entries.actionSubtitle: Balance, config, server safety, and enchant scaling
details: Fixed the Conqueror unlock requirement so it now follows the configured Armament and Ryuo level requirements instead of forcing Ryuo to level 50.
Updated the default Conqueror unlock path to Armament level 25 and Ryuo level 25.
Added server-side charge validation for major charged Haki sword skills so stale releases are rejected more safely on multiplayer servers.
Charged skill validation now tracks player identity, dimension, hotbar slot, held item, item damage, and active Haki coating mode.
Applied the stronger charge context checks to Tiger Hunt, Dragon Twister, Lion's Requiem, Six Paths Severance, Billion-Fold World, Trichiliocosm, Asura Silver Mist, and Asura Dead Man's Game.
Added clearer failed-charge feedback messages so players are told when a charge was too short or broke because the weapon/coating changed.
Softened early Asura balance by increasing the Novice duration and reducing the early cooldown curve.
Cleaned up Asura early-unlock costs so Silver Mist and Dead Man's Game scale more logically after Asura Mode.
Improved Asura resource safety so Ki and stamina are checked before spending, preventing stamina from being wasted when Ki payment fails.
Added a compact Next Unlocks helper line to the Haki controls/progression GUI.
Added a new skills.haki_techniques config category for sword technique balance.
Sword skill cooldowns, stamina costs, Ki scaling, minimum costs, and charge timings can now be tuned from config instead of being fully hardcoded.

Configurable technique balance now covers Sword Slash, Multi Slash, Dragon Rising, Phoenix Rend, Pound Phoenix, Tiger Hunt, Dragon Twister, Lion's Requiem, Six Paths, Trichiliocosm, Asura activation, Asura Silver Mist, and Asura Dead Man's Game.
Added shorter in-game config display names for long Haki progression and Haki technique config keys.
Added hover tooltips for Haki config entries showing the full internal key and a brief explanation of what each option controls.
Added the custom Haki Edge enchantment for Haki-compatible weapons.
Haki Edge uses a HyperText-styled display name and can appear on compatible weapons or rare custom enchanted books.
Haki Edge increases sword skill damage and active Haki damage, with separate config values for per-level scaling and maximum bonus caps.
Haki Edge scaling applies to major sword arts including Phoenix Rend, Pound Phoenix, Dragon Rising, Tiger Hunt, Dragon Twister, Lion's Requiem, Six Paths, Trichiliocosm, and Asura sword variants.
Haki Edge also boosts coated direct melee hits and Haki sweep-style damage while the weapon has an active Haki mode.
Added weapon tooltip lines showing the current Haki Edge sword skill bonus and active Haki damage bonus.
Fixed a Pound Phoenix compile issue caused by mismatched method capitalization in the configurable technique balance pass.

Haki Edge increases sword skill damage and active Haki damage, with separate config values for per-level scaling and maximum bonus caps.
Haki Edge scaling applies to major sword arts including Phoenix Rend, Pound Phoenix, Dragon Rising, Tiger Hunt, Dragon Twister, Lion's Requiem, Six Paths, Trichiliocosm, and Asura sword variants.
Haki Edge also boosts coated direct melee hits and Haki sweep-style damage while the weapon has an active Haki mode.
Added weapon tooltip lines showing the current Haki Edge sword skill bonus and active Haki damage bonus.
Fixed a Pound Phoenix compile issue caused by mismatched method capitalization in the configurable technique balance pass.

entries.title: Pound Phoenix Added + Stacked Cooldown Lore Polish
entries.summary: A new early HexHaki sword projectile has been added with evolving Pound Phoenix stages, Phoenix Rend has been sharpened into a crossing Iai dash, and socketed orb cooldown effects now stack properly with a visible total cooldown line in item lore.
details: Added Pound Phoenix as a new early HexHaki sword skill unlocked through the Sword Style path.
Pound Phoenix uses Caps Lock + Left Ctrl + Right Mouse, while Phoenix Rend remains on Left Ctrl + Right Mouse.
Pound Phoenix progresses through mastery-style stages instead of raw Sword Style level jumps.
Current Pound Phoenix stage names include 36 Pound Phoenix, 72 Pound Phoenix, 108 Pound Phoenix, 360 Pound Phoenix, 720 Pound Phoenix, and 1080 Pound Phoenix.
Pound Phoenix acts as a ranged compressed-air sword projectile, giving Sword Style an earlier ranged pressure option before later large-scale techniques.

Pound Phoenix visuals shift based on active Haki coating: golden air pressure by default, hardened dark edges with Armament, blue-white flowing force with Ryuo, and black-red lightning pressure with Conqueror.
Phoenix Rend has been reworked toward a fast Iai-style crossing dash instead of overlapping with Pound Phoenix's ranged identity.
Phoenix Rend now performs multiple crossing cuts, scaling from smaller multi-hit slashes into a Crossing the Six Paths-style dash at higher mastery.
Added bite-mark style slash particles to Phoenix Rend so the dash leaves a sharper carved crossing impact effect.
Fixed the Pound Phoenix and Phoenix Rend input conflict so Ctrl + Right Mouse keeps Phoenix Rend, while Caps + Ctrl + Right Mouse cleanly fires Pound Phoenix.
Orb cooldown effects now stack together across socketed gems and direct orb sources instead of only using the strongest single cooldown roll.
Total cooldown reduction is capped at 75 percent to prevent cooldowns from becoming effectively free.
Socketed item lore now displays a Total Skill Cooldown line so players can see their combined cooldown reduction directly on the orb page.
Existing socketed weapons may need one socket refresh or re-socket action before the new total cooldown lore line appears.
Added a JRMC-style timed buff HUD icon path for temporary buff effects so active boosts can show a status-style countdown on screen.

entries.title: Custom enchantments expanded
entries.summary: Sweeping Edge, Hex Luck, Sword Mastery book drops, and visible modern sweep particles are now part of the Haki combat enchantment line.
entries.actionSubtitle: Sweep, reach, drops, and luck scaling
details: Added a custom Sweeping Edge enchantment for 1.7.10. It can appear from the enchantment table up to Level V.
Sweeping Edge adds modern-style sweeping combat. At higher levels, successful melee hits can trigger a forward AoE sweep and extended melee reach up to 7 blocks.
Sweeping Edge now plays visible modern particle effects on successful primary hits, using sweep_attack, gust, small_gust, enchanted_hit, trail, flash, and enchanted hit sparks.
Custom enchanted books can now rarely drop from eligible vanilla hostile mobs, DBC entities, and NPCDBC-style entities.
Supported custom book drops include Hex Luck I-X, Sword Mastery I-X, and Sweeping Edge I-V.
Hex Luck now increases HexOrb drop odds and also improves the odds of custom enchanted book drops.
Custom enchant names use HexText/HyperText styling for a more unique visual identity.

entries.title: CustomNPC HyperText editor FPS guard
entries.summary: CustomNPC manager/list screens now bypass live HyperText rendering so styled quest/category/dialog lists do not tank FPS while editing.
details: Added a targeted heavy-editor detector for CustomNPC manager/list GUIs.
Quest, dialog, faction, tag, transporter, recipe, and similar manager screens now use the cheap vanilla font path for list rows.
HyperText controls in those editor lists are stripped to readable text instead of being animated every frame.
Player-facing CustomNPC dialogs and explicit dialog text-area bridge rendering remain allowed.
This is a focused FPS fix; it does not change Haki, Asura, Dragon Twister, or combat balance.

entries.title: Dragon Twister fuller Haki body fill
entries.summary: Added a fuller sustained tornado body for every Haki variant by layering a soft cloud/smoke fill inside the existing tornado shell.
details: Startup swirl was left unchanged.
Added a sustained-only body-fill layer for all Dragon Twister variants.
Used a mix of light legacy cloud/smoke and additive modern fill particles.
Ryuo, Conqueror, and Asura each receive their own styled inner body fill.
No gameplay, damage, pull, cooldown, or EXP values were changed.

entries.title: Sword Mastery enchantment and native DBC EXP eligibility
entries.summary: Sword Mastery now boosts combat-earned Haki and Sword progression, while every genuine native JRMCore/DBC combat mob qualifies for at least the High reward branch without turning every early-saga enemy into a physical boss.
details: Sword Mastery is a new HyperText-styled weapon enchantment. Normal enchanting is centered on levels I-V, while levels VI-X require exceptionally rare exact high-power enchanting rolls.
The default progression bonus is 2% per enchantment level: Sword Mastery V grants 10% and Sword Mastery X grants 20% more combat-earned Haki, Sword Style, Sword bank, and technique mastery EXP.
Raw enchantment NBT remains supported up to Minecraft 1.7.10's signed-short level limit of 32,767, with overflow protection and fractional carry for small EXP awards.
Fixed Dragon Ball wish deposits, command grants, and master rewards are excluded from Sword Mastery so the enchantment cannot multiply non-combat progression rewards.
Every genuine native JRMCore/Dragon Block C combat NPC now grants progression EXP and uses at least the High reward branch. Normalized 600+ power enemies still receive the full Boss branch.
Vanilla mobs, CustomNPCs, NPCDBC handling, Ninjin entities, summons, dummies, explicit no-EXP flags, and the existing anti-farming system were not loosened by this pass.

entries.title: Blackblaze Katana first-person render alignment pass
entries.summary: Blackblaze now borrows the Spiral Guard Katana first-person framing style so the oversized nodachi actually stays visible on-screen instead of hiding most of the weapon in first person.
details: The Blackblaze Katana main-hand first-person transform now uses the Spiral Guard Katana camera framing style instead of the previous Big Bertha-style first-person test position.
First-person offhand and camera-space offhand views were updated to the matching Spiral Guard style so dual-wield and Battlegear/Hex offhand handling stay visually consistent.
Blocking offsets were converted to the new framing so the weapon still shifts into guard cleanly without pushing most of the blade off-screen.
A small first-person hilt pivot fine-tune was added to keep more of the blade and fiery edge visible in the viewport.
Third-person placement, custom Blackblaze model geometry, Haki overlay rendering, and animated fire layers were left unchanged in this pass.

entries.title: Dragon Twister anchor & EXP HUD correction
entries.summary: Haki and sword bars now use their own earned EXP, while Dragon Twister forms where the opening slash connects and pulls nearby targets into its persistent AoE.
details: Visible Haki, Sword Style, technique, and quick-popup bars now use the local track or skill EXP value instead of displaying an Auto 0/max value after purchased progression.
Shared Sword EXP remains a separate purchase pool and no longer visually fills every Haki track bar.
Dragon Twister now anchors its persistent tornado at the nearest entity struck by the opening slash; casts that miss use a closer fallback endpoint instead of the maximum range.
The tornado has a larger outer pull ring that drags nearby entities into the damaging AoE core over repeated pulses.
Conqueror and Asura Dragon Twister variants add a black-rope particle dragon coiling inside the tornado, including red eyes, lightning accents, a snout, and horns.

entries.title: Haki HUD restoration & Dragon Twister field
entries.summary: Hybrid progression bars are restored across the Haki GUI and quick EXP popup, while Dragon Twister now opens with a slash and leaves a persistent damaging tornado at its endpoint.
details: The Haki and Sword Skills GUI once again fills progress bars from the further of automatic progression or spendable bank progression instead of visually falling back to Auto EXP only.
Haki track bars include converted shared Sword EXP when the track is unlocked, while locked Ryuo and Conqueror rows remain visually inactive.
The compact mastery popup returns to stable packet-driven values and now receives the total spendable Haki track amount so its bar better matches the full GUI.
Dragon Twister now releases an opening slash that summons a persistent tornado at the endpoint rather than resolving as a one-tick corridor attack.
The summoned vortex repeatedly damages, pulls, spins, and lifts targets for several seconds before collapsing into a final launch.

Base, Armament, Ryuo, Black Rope Conqueror, and Asura versions use different field durations, pressure strength, particle palettes, and collapse force while preserving the existing keybind, mastery, cooldown, and Ki-cost systems.

entries.title: Dragon Twister vortex & HUD polish
entries.summary: Dragon Twister now has a stronger vortex identity, a dedicated HUD icon, refreshed variant naming, and the quick mastery popup should better reflect real Haki progress.
details: The quick Haki EXP popup now reads live mastery values so its progress bars and bank text stay closer to the full GUI instead of underselling track progress.
Dragon Twister was reworked toward a forward cyclone lane so it feels more like a real traveling vortex instead of a flatter slash-like hit shape.
Targets caught in Dragon Twister are pulled into the lane, spun, carried forward, and launched more clearly, with stronger pressure in Ryuo, Conqueror, and Asura states.

Variant naming was refreshed around the requested fantasy: Dragon Twister, Great Dragon Twister, Great Dragon Twister: Ryuo, Black Rope Great Dragon Twister, and Asura: Black Rope Nine-Headed Dragon Twister.
Dragon Twister now has its own cooldown/GUI icon instead of borrowing Dragon Rising's icon, and the technique tooltip text was updated to describe the vortex-focused behavior.

entries.title: Haki & Asura combat expansion
entries.summary: Native DBC Ki efficiency, rank-based Asura upkeep, transformed sword arts, cleaner controls, responsive HUD/GUI work, and the new Dragon Twister technique are now part of the current Haki combat line.
details: Ki Fist and Ki Protection now use their own native DBC combat paths. Each level grants 7.5% directional Ki-cost reduction, with JRMCore levels clamped to 0-10 and a 75% maximum reduction at level 10.
Asura now has rank-based duration, Ki drain, and reactivation cooldown. Perfected Asura has no fixed duration and remains active only while the player's Ki pool can sustain its recurring drain.

Asura transforms the regular sword arsenal: Three-Realm Sever, Ninefold Calamity, Hellfire Phoenix Funeral, Nine-Claw Hunt, Dragon Crown Rising, Demonic Lion's Requiem, Nine Paths Severance, and Nine Worlds Collapse.
The Haki progression and Controls screens now fit long technique names more safely at smaller GUI scales, and the shared cooldown shelf shows transformed Asura names without cutting them off.

Final original-Asura inputs: Silver Mist uses Caps Lock + 2nd Fn + Left Alt + held Right Mouse; Dead Man's Game uses Caps Lock + Left Alt + held Right Mouse; Billion-Fold World keeps Sneak + 2nd Fn + Left Alt + Right Mouse.

New Sword Style technique: Dragon Twister. Hold Caps Lock + Right Mouse and release after READY. Base wind, Armament, Ryuo, Conqueror, and Asura versions have distinct radius, pull, launch, hit-count, color, and impact behavior.
While Asura is active, Dragon Twister becomes Asura: Nine-Headed Dragon Twister, expanding into nine linked cyclone strikes with a larger execution field and stronger final launch.

Optional CustomNPC+ player animations are included for Silver Mist, Dead Man's Game, Dragon Twister, and its Nine-Headed Asura transformation. The bridge is reflection-only, so combat still works if CustomNPC+ animation playback is unavailable.

entries.title: Asura Transformation Polish and Transformed Sword Techniques
entries.summary: Asura now has dedicated activation and exhaustion transitions, synchronized spectral Haki coatings, and transformed versions of Tiger Hunt, Dragon Rising, Lion's Requiem, and Six Paths Severance.
details: Asura now forms through a short activation sequence, ends through a controlled exhaustion transition, and never runs its activation and cooldown states at the same time.
Spectral weapon copies visually inherit the held weapon's Armament, Ryuo, or Conqueror coating while retaining one authoritative real weapon and damage source.

Tiger Hunt becomes Nine-Claw Hunt, Dragon Rising becomes Asura Dragon Rising, Six Paths becomes the nine-strike Nine Paths Severance, and Lion's Requiem becomes Demonic Lion's Requiem while Asura is active.

Transformed techniques reuse their normal unlocks, ranks, cooldowns, EXP, and anti-farming rules. Silver Mist now uses 2nd Fn + Left Alt + middle mouse during Asura so Nine-Claw Hunt keeps the normal Tiger Hunt input.

entries.title: Orb Fall Guard, Multi-Target Mastery EXP, and Skill Controls
entries.summary: Damage-triggered orb effects no longer activate from fall events, multi-target sword techniques now reward each valid enemy, and the Haki GUI includes a complete controls reference for every current skill.
details: Fall and DBC/JRMCore landing notifications are excluded from damage-triggered orb passives, dodges, barriers, shard gains, and defensive proc cooldowns.
Sword techniques can now award technique, Sword Style, and active-Haki EXP for as many as 12 unique valid targets in one cast while retaining repeat-target anti-farming protection.
Vanilla mobs, CustomNPCs, DBC/NPCDBC entities, Ninjin entities, strong enemies, and bosses continue to use combat-strength scaling for hit and kill rewards.

The Haki progression GUI now has a Controls tab with the live 2nd Fn binding and input combinations for Sword Slash, Multi Slash, Phoenix Rend, Dragon Rising, Tiger Hunt, Lion's Requiem, Six Paths, Billion-Fold World, Asura, Silver Mist, and Dead Man's Game.

entries.title: Dragon Rising Expansion and Axe Combat Support
entries.summary: Dragon Rising now remains active for a much longer multi-hit sequence, scales its duration and hit count through the different Haki types, and keeps targets suspended until the final up-smash launch. Skill hit-count debug messages are now disabled by default, while axes and battle axes gained yellow cleave effects with special hybrid colors when Haki is active.
entries.actionSubtitle: Dragon Rising and axe combat pass
details: Dragon Rising now deals damage throughout nearly the entire visible particle animation instead of ending its damage sequence while the effect is still active.
Targets caught by Dragon Rising are tracked through the sequence, repeatedly carried upward, and launched strongly by the final up-smash hit.
The normal Dragon Rising sequence now performs 8 hits over roughly 2.15 seconds.
Armament Haki increases Dragon Rising to 10 hits over roughly 2.65 seconds.
Hardening increases Dragon Rising to 12 hits over roughly 3.15 seconds.
Ryuo increases Dragon Rising to 14 hits over roughly 3.65 seconds.
Conqueror's Haki increases Dragon Rising to 17 hits over roughly 4.4 seconds.
Hakai provides the longest version with 20 hits over roughly 5.15 seconds.
Dragon Rising damage was redistributed across the longer sequence so the increased hit count does not multiply the original total damage uncontrollably.
Skill release and hit-count chat lines for Dragon Rising, Multi Slash, and Phoenix Rend are now controlled by a debug setting that is disabled by default.
Important gameplay warnings such as insufficient Ki, insufficient stamina, invalid weapons, and active cooldowns remain visible.
Axes and battle axes can now use the standard held-right-click attack path as Axe Cleave.
Axe Cleave uses wider, heavier, and slightly slower waves with stronger knockback than standard sword slashes.
Normal axe and battle-axe attacks use bright gold and yellow visual effects.
Armament-coated axes use a hybrid yellow-and-black effect.
Hardening-coated axes use gold, white, and black effects.
Ryuo-coated axes use yellow and cyan flowing energy.
Conqueror-coated axes use yellow effects mixed with red and black Haki accents.
Active held-weapon Haki lore now recognizes supported axes and battle axes while continuing to remain hidden whenever the held weapon's Haki coating is switched off.
Possible future axe skills include Sundering Wheel, Earthsplitter Drop, and Titan Guillotine.

entries.title: Perfect Core proc HUD, transparent bars, and orb VFX refresh
entries.summary: Perfect Core now displays its own gem icon when it borrows other orb proc effects, the proc HUD bars were made more transparent with fewer hard border lines, fire target visuals were softened, and older vanilla-heavy orb particle effects received modern particle accents.
entries.actionSubtitle: Perfect Core and orb visual polish
details: Perfect Core proc HUD: borrowed Void, Abyss, Dream, Ocean, Glitch, and Astral effects now prefer the Perfect Core gem icon on the HUD when Perfect Core is the equipped source.

Perfect Core proc list expanded: the shared passive checks now allow Perfect Core to run the current Dreamscape, Crystalline Ocean, Glitch Prism, Abyss, Astral, Void, Fractured-style low-body, Fire Punch, and Perfect Core native effects from one socketed source.
Void proc tuning: original Void family passive proc rates were lowered slightly so Gravity Well, Entropy, and Abyss Mark do not trigger as aggressively during normal combat.
HUD polish: shared orb cooldown bars and Dream/Astral proc shelf bars now use a glassier transparent look with much softer outlines, highlights, and scan-line accents.

Fire visual polish: target burn no longer forces the opaque vanilla fire overlay by default; target impact and DoT particles now lean on the same translucent flame/ember opacity used by the first-person fire-hand visuals.
Particle refresh: older vanilla-heavy orb visuals in the shared controller gained modern glow, sculk, spark, and soft accent particles while keeping vanilla fallback particles for 1.7.10 readability.

entries.title: Astral Prism skip chain, Star Tornado field, and rare 100% orb rolls
entries.summary: Astral Prism's dodge package was expanded so Orbit Step can perform a true multi-skip counter, Star Tornado now lingers as a pulling damage-over-time particle tornado, and ordinary percent orb rolls gained a tiny chance to land an exact 100% stat line.
entries.actionSubtitle: Astral combat and orb roll polish
details: Astral Orbit Step now starts a delayed multi-skip sequence instead of only doing an instant single reposition: the player blinks around the attacker up to 6 times with short gaps between skips, then finishes with a counter strike and astral particle burst.
Fixed the Astral defensive proc order so a failed Starforce roll no longer blocks Orbit Step from trying on the same incoming hit, making the multi-skip move much easier to actually see in combat.
Astral Star Tornado now creates an active tornado field for several seconds instead of only doing one instant AoE burst.
Enemies inside Star Tornado are pulled inward, spun around the funnel, lightly lifted, and damaged over time while the particle tornado remains active.
Star Tornado visuals now keep ticking while active, using astral purple/cyan spark, glow, witch-magic, and falling star-style particles before ending in a burst.
All ordinary percent orb stat rolls now have a tiny jackpot chance to roll an exact 100% line. Existing socket handling preserves 100 as a true 100% value instead of collapsing it to 1%.

entries.title: HyperText Prefix/Suffix Width and CustomNPC Wrapping Fix
entries.summary: A new HexFontRenderer pass fixed the long-running prefix and suffix smushing issue caused by HyperText display names, while also restoring the CustomNPC HyperText text-area and wrapping support.
details: Fixed the player prefix/suffix spacing issue where Essentials/GroupManager display names could look crushed or overlapped when HyperText was rendered through the custom HexFontRenderer.
Updated HexFontRenderer width handling so HyperText names measure closer to how they actually render, especially with bold styled text and colored prefixes or suffixes.
Improved display-name compatibility for EssentialsChat-style formats such as '<{DISPLAYNAME}> {MESSAGE}', allowing HyperText inside the name without breaking chat spacing.
Restored the CustomNPC HyperText pass for dialog text, text areas, and wrapping behavior so longer custom text no longer wraps incorrectly in NPC GUI screens.
Removed the fragile inner TextAreaState dependency from the CustomNPC HyperText hook path, preventing the previous missing-class crash when opening CustomNPC dialog management screens.
Bundled the CustomNPC wrapping/text-area fix and the prefix/suffix width fix together as a source patch so the text rendering chain is safer and more consistent.

entries.title: Dream Gem Effects Complete + Legacy Totem DBC Fix
entries.summary: The Dream Gem/Orb effect chain has been completed with seven passive effects, animated Dream HUD support, Reverie status-style icons, Nightmare Bloom visuals, and a DBC-safe Legacy Totem fix that prevents false activations from low vanilla health.
details: Finished the full Dream Gem/Orb passive effect set: Dream Echo, Lucid Recovery, Dream Slip, False Awakening, Dream Fracture, Reverie Chain, and Nightmare Bloom.
Dream Echo can repeat a hit shortly after impact with a weaker dream echo strike and improved glow, enchant, portal, shimmer, and afterimage-style particles.
Lucid Recovery now checks DBC Body thresholds, restores Body/Ki/Stamina during its recovery window, uses a cooldown, and hides or resumes its HUD properly when the Dream source is swapped.
Dream Slip now catches damage through safer DBC-aware attack/hurt handling, reduces incoming damage, plays UI dodge-style feedback, and uses dream shimmer particles.
False Awakening adds a weaker dream-themed near-death save with a long cooldown, small recovery, brief protection, and modern dream/totem-style particles.
Dream Fracture now applies a soft utility debuff that makes targets deal less damage and take more damage, using the same all-damage-path handling proven by the Fracture Brew test item.
Reverie Chain adds a short lucid rhythm window where the next hit can trigger a random bonus such as cooldown refund, Ki refund, Stamina refund, Body refund, bonus hit, or haze mark.
Reverie Chain received custom status-style icons and now renders its active bonus near the JRM/DBC status-effect icon area instead of only using the Dream cooldown shelf.

Nightmare Bloom now plants a dream seed that swirls through and around the target, loops back several times, then blooms into a small dream explosion with soft weaken effects and a Body refund for the Dream holder.
Dream HUD support was expanded with animated dream bars, Dream Gem icon usage, source-aware clearing/resuming, and cooldown rows for the completed passive chain.
Fixed the Legacy Totem DBC interaction so it no longer pops every hit just because vanilla health is low while DBC Body is still alive.
For DBC players, Legacy Totem activation is now gated around true lethal danger instead of vanilla-health-only damage checks.

entries.title: Orb Effects, Modern Particles, Slash Scaling, and Server Fixes
entries.summary: The latest HexColorText passes expanded modern particle support, improved Void Relic effects, lowered cooldown reduction caps for stacking balance, fixed several HUD/icon issues, and improved server-side slash activation for custom weapons.
details: <rune><grad #B994FF #63F7FF #FFFFFF #9B6CFF scroll=0.18>Modern particle support was expanded with a full particle catalog, JSON frame mapping, aliases, presets, and script APIs for effects like dragon_breath, sculk_charge, sonic_boom, totem_of_undying, sweep_attack, and more.</grad></rune>

<rune><grad #7A35FF #B994FF #63F7FF #FFFFFF scroll=0.20>Void Rend now uses modern and classic particle layers, applies a chance-based DoT, and can trigger upgraded Void-style visuals through Void Relic effects.</grad></rune>

<rune><grad #3A0A66 #7A35FF #D6B3FF #FFFFFF scroll=0.16>Void Relic gained rare Void Explosion support, using modern particles and multiple explosion hits where higher hit counts reduce individual hit damage.</grad></rune>

<rune><grad #63F7FF #9B6CFF #FFFFFF #76FFB8 scroll=0.18>Perfect Core and Fractured threshold messages were cleaned up so they trigger on threshold changes instead of every Body increment or decrement, now showing actual Body or HP values with brighter HyperText styling.</grad></rune>

<rune><grad #FFE27A #FFFFFF #76FFB8 #63F7FF scroll=0.20>Cooldown reduction caps were reduced again for stacking balance: Crystalline Ocean and most next-gen gems now cap much lower, while Dream Gem remains higher but still nerfed.</grad></rune>

<rune><grad #FFFFFF #9B6CFF #63F7FF #FFFFFF scroll=0.17>Haki Slash, Multi Slash, and Reaping Wave now scale from a DBC stat formula focused mostly on Dexterity, with Strength and WillPower contributing as secondary stats.</grad></rune>

<rune><grad #B994FF #FFFFFF #63F7FF #9B6CFF scroll=0.18>The slash input handler now supports raw right-click hold as a fallback, helping custom weapons that qualify for slash effects but do not properly enter vanilla blocking state on servers.</grad></rune>

<rune><grad #76FFB8 #FFFFFF #B994FF #63F7FF scroll=0.16>HexMaster GUI packet initialization was improved for dedicated servers, addressing cases where /hexmaster said it was opening the GUI but nothing appeared.</grad></rune>

<rune><grad #FFD966 #FFFFFF #76FFB8 #63F7FF scroll=0.18>Sign FPS rendering now keeps targeted signs vanilla by default, making SignShop setup safer while preserving cached sign rendering for large sign walls.</grad></rune>

entries.title: Next-Gen Orb Balance, DBC Body Regen, and Totem Death Bypass Fix
entries.summary: Next-gen orb cooldown reduction was brought down with new per-orb caps, pulsed DBC Body regeneration was added, and the Totem of Undying now uses a stronger JRMCore revive-bypass flow so it can save players before Otherworld death handling takes over.
details: Next-gen orb cooldown reduction was reduced again and now clamps to safer per-orb caps instead of letting old or high rolls keep oversized cooldown values.
Dream Gem keeps the highest cooldown-reduction identity at up to 64%, Crystalline Ocean Gem now caps at 45%, and the rest of the next-gen orb family is capped at 60% or lower.

Next-gen orbs gained a pulsed DBC Body regeneration effect. Instead of constantly healing every tick, the effect briefly restores Body, stops, waits a few seconds, then starts another small regen pulse.

The Totem of Undying now catches lethal damage earlier and forces a stronger JRMCore alive-state guard so it can prevent DBC/JRMCore death handling from immediately sending the player to Otherworld after the totem is consumed.

The totem revive path now refreshes vanilla health, restores DBC Body above zero, clears dangerous effects, resets death/damaged flags, and keeps the player alive for a short guard window after activation.

entries.title: Haki Weapon Texture Pass: Vanilla, DBC, CustomNPC+, Chocolate Quest, Plugin, and More
entries.summary: The Haki weapon coating system was expanded across vanilla and several major mod weapon sets, including CustomNPC+, Dragon Block C, Chocolate Quest, MrCrayfish Furniture, and ThePlugin. Static and animated weapon textures now have Armament, Hardening, Ryuo, and Conqueror variants where supported.
details: Vanilla item Haki rendering was fixed first: active Haki now uses stitched item-atlas icons for inventory, first-person, and third-person views instead of reverting to vanilla textures or white-square fallback renders when Slash or Multi Slash fires.

CustomNPC+ received Haki textures for the confirmed melee weapon set, including swords, broadswords, scythes, daggers, spears, tridents, halberds, glaives, battle axes, maces, warhammers, claws, katanas, rapiers, sabers, kukris, and other generic attack weapons.

Dragon Block C received a normal item-icon Haki pass for its sword, axe, spear, club, hammer, blade, and handle items, plus an extended model-texture pass for special rendered weapons like Katana, Brave Sword, Z Sword, Dimension Sword, Evil Spear, and Power Pole.

Chocolate Quest received Haki textures for real ItemCQBlade-style melee weapons, including swords, big swords, daggers, spears, hook sword, and the Bull battle axe, while guns, staves, shields, armor, and utility items were skipped to avoid accidental coating.

The mixed utility-mod scan only found one true generic-attack weapon target: the MrCrayfish Furniture knife. It now has all four Haki texture modes while non-weapon blocks, tools, render libraries, and chest upgrades were left untouched.

ThePlugin received the largest Haki expansion: hundreds of registered melee/generic-attack Plugin weapons were added to the Haki texture bank, including preserved .mcmeta animation files for animated weapon textures.
Each supported weapon family now has four Haki modes: Armament, Hardening, Ryuo, and Conqueror. These modes are intended to match the existing weapon Haki state rather than replacing item behavior.
The Haki renderer keeps using the stitched-atlas path and mod-aware held transforms so coated weapons should keep their normal inventory, first-person, and third-person presentation while active.
Ranged weapons, spell items, shields, armor, vanity items, render-only entity weapons, and utility tools were intentionally skipped unless they were confirmed as true melee or generic-attack items.

entries.title: Hit Skill Script Cleanup: Counters, Time Stop, and Knockback Fixes
entries.summary: The Hit-style moveset script received another cleanup pass focused on counter behavior, Time Stop escape handling, safer cooldown display logic, and more reliable knockback after frozen-time damage resolves.
details: Cleaned up several script bugs from the large Hit moveset file, including duplicate logic, mismatched helper names, unsafe timer references, and places where old debug or fallback paths could conflict with newer skill behavior.
Flash Fist Crush was adjusted so the normal Lv1–5 counter path properly reflects damage back onto the attacker instead of only arming visuals or failing to credit the reflected hit.
Tremor Pulse Lv1–5 was adjusted so its normal counter path also reflects the attacker correctly while keeping Over Heaven / Lv6 behavior separate as the healing-style variant.
Counter moves now include knockback on successful reflected hits, making Flash Fist Crush and Tremor Pulse feel more like real counterattacks instead of only delayed damage pops.
Time Stop escape handling was reviewed so escaped players can break free, bank damage against the caster during the escape window, and then refreeze correctly if time has not fully resumed.
Time Stop end handling was improved so stored frozen-time damage, escape-window damage, overlays, countdowns, and cleanup paths resolve more safely when time resumes.
Frozen-time knockback was made more reliable after final stored damage is applied, including cases where the stored damage is high enough to nearly kill or fully defeat the target.
The cooldown HUD behavior was left mostly intact because the cooldown timer setup was already intentionally structured that way.

entries.title: Legacy Items, Totem, Slash Cooldowns, and Texture Fixes
entries.summary: A new legacy item cleanup pass restored missing food textures, fixed the Piss Bucket visuals, added the Totem of Undying, separated normal Slash and Multi Slash cooldowns, increased slash range, and cleaned up several orb and food behavior issues.
details: Missing legacy item textures were re-imported from the old cursed source so the broken magenta-black placeholder icons should now display correctly.
The Piss Bucket now uses its proper legacy bucket texture and keeps the custom yellow piss-fluid still/flowing textures instead of looking like a normal water bucket.
The Totem of Undying was added as a HexColor Text item and moved into the main HexColor Text creative tab instead of the Legacy Useless tab.
The Totem of Undying can cancel one fatal hit, consume itself, restore health, clear harmful potion effects, and attempt to restore DBC Body.
Normal Slash and Multi Slash now use separate cooldowns, so the regular slash and Sneak + Right Click multi-combo no longer lock each other out.
Slash range was increased for both normal Slash and Multi Slash so the visual waves have a better chance to connect with targets.
Multi Slash HUD labeling was separated from the regular slash label, showing Multi Slash or Multi Reaping when the combo skill is on cooldown.

entries.title: Visual Dev: Haki slash fixes, Black Coffin / Dragon Fist refresh, HUD polish, and new gem rolls
entries.summary: The 1.21.11 asset refresh pass has been folded into the current mod source with Black Coffin visuals, Dragon Fist effects, cooldown HUD upgrades, new animated gems, and several Haki slash fixes. The latest pass also fixes the slash/blocking jitter and makes slash waves follow the player's look pitch instead of staying mostly flat.
details: Black Coffin received a visual refresh using sculk-style charge, soul, forcefield, shriek, flash, and discharge-style overlays. The goal was to make the move feel darker and more modern without changing its core damage behavior.

Dragon Fist received new visual additions using sonic-boom rings, gust trails, small-gust overlays, flash bursts, and impact-style explosion overlays. This makes the rush and hit moments read stronger in combat.

Cooldown HUDs were refreshed with modern boss-bar style textures for Black Coffin, Dragon Fist, and Haki Slash / Reaping Wave. These are lightweight HUD textures and should not bring back the old sign/shop FPS problem.
The correct dev_assets folder was updated with the new Black Coffin, Dragon Fist, HUD, and gem textures so the dev environment can render the new visuals correctly.
New animated gems were added to the mod and included in the gem/orb drop pool. Their tooltip preview was updated to show the new random stat roll behavior.

New gem stat rolls now use random DBC .Multi stats with values from -5% up to +15%. Rolls can include one stat, multiple stats, or rarely all five main stats. Effects are still left for a future design pass.
Haki slash waves were updated to follow the player's full look direction using yaw and pitch, so slashes can now travel upward, downward, or diagonally based on where the player is aiming.

The Haki slash blocking jitter was fixed by removing the forced swing call from the slash fire path and adding a small release buffer / cooldown message throttle. Blocking should no longer spaz out when the slash key logic is involved.
Earlier Haki slash compile issues were cleaned up too, including the misplaced @Override in EntityHakiSlashWave and missing helper-method calls in WeaponHakiSlashController.

entries.title: Weapon Dev: Phoenix stable, Rose Scythe sweep work, and blade model cleanup
entries.summary: Phoenix Nodachi is in a much better in-hand state, the Hyper Energy Scythe has progressed into a staged rose/magenta weapon with sweep/AoE experiments, and the oversized purple-orange blade line is being rebuilt with cleaner Blockbench/dev-asset workflow. Current focus is now model polish, item registration, and keeping heavy Blockbench files out of the runtime jar.
details: Cursed Blade status: the current in-game version is acceptable for now. Deep Cursed Blade work can stay paused while newer weapon work focuses on Phoenix Nodachi, Hyper Energy Scythe, and the purple-orange Cosmic Ember Blade direction.

Phoenix Nodachi status: the weapon reached a much better in-hand state after placement, icon, guard, connection, and cutting-edge direction fixes. Future Phoenix work should be small positioning or texture polish instead of full rewrites.

Phoenix placement lesson: Dragon Block C katana-style rendering helped confirm that the handle and blade need a clean shared local axis, with the handle passing through the hand pivot rather than floating from the shoulder or hilt root.

Hyper Energy Scythe status: the scythe line moved into a 4-stage rose/magenta evolution concept. Stage-based damage, visual scale, sweep cooldown, AoE range, AoE damage, and double-slash chance were tested.

Scythe sweep work: the sweep effect evolved from small rose particles into a larger custom rose/flat crescent slash. Several placement passes tested 1.9-style sweep, Getsuga-like flat crescent behavior, crosshair anchoring, and stage-based cooldowns.

Scythe combat tuning: the current staged sweep test uses different cooldowns and AoE values per stage, with a small double-slash chance. The final stage remains intended to be the strongest form and should keep the highest damage identity.

Scythe visual note: the inventory sprites remain the strongest scythe asset and should be preserved as the target identity: dark purple-black metal, rose/magenta energy, glowing head core, crystal shards, and crescent energy blade.

Scythe model status: held-model work is still not final. The rough prism/sprite/Blockbench attempts helped test direction, but the final scythe still needs a proper model pass that matches the strong inventory sprite silhouette.

DBC Fn key idea: future custom weapon skills can piggyback DBC's existing Fn key as a modifier. For example, if the custom skill key is B, the real trigger can become DBC Fn + B, while still letting DBC own its normal key handling.

Cosmic Ember Blade direction: a new oversized purple-orange blade concept was explored as a zanpakuto-like great blade with dark cosmic purple body, ember-orange cutting edge, wrapped handle, and winged/angelic guard details.

Cosmic Ember Blade model status: multiple Blockbench test files were created, but the current issue is that the hilt still reads too much like a starburst instead of real wings, and the blade tip needs to be centered and cleaned up.

Winged hilt target: the guard should read as angel wings, with feather-like stepped voxel layers sweeping outward and slightly upward/downward. It should not look like a generic star, cross, or spike cluster.
Blade tip target: the tip needs to be centered on the blade axis and taper naturally into the silhouette, instead of looking like an offset cap or stacked block cluster.

Blockbench workflow update: .bbmodel files, model references, and experimental model sources should live under dev_assets/blockbench instead of src/main/resources so they stay editable without being packed into the runtime jar.

Jar-size cleanup: moving Blockbench models out of runtime resources is the correct approach. Only actual in-game textures, lang files, sounds, and runtime assets should remain under src/main/resources.

Current source organization: a runtime-clean source zip was made with model files moved out of src/main/resources, plus a dev-assets pack containing Blockbench files for editing outside the built mod jar.

Important item note: adding .bbmodel files or dev assets does not automatically add new weapons to the mod. If the new weapons do not show in HexColorText, the next source task is item registration, creative tab entries, icon paths, names, and renderer hookup.

Future model patch rule: continue using the latest uploaded source as baseline, keep Java 6 compatibility, avoid wildcard imports, and do not bundle runtime-only mod jars or dev-only Blockbench files into the final mod jar.

entries.title: NEI Tooltip Marker Fixed
entries.summary: Fixed the hidden NEI tooltip marker that caused styled HexText item names to show a tiny smushed tail.
details: Fixed the long-standing smushed tail artifact on styled item tooltip names.
The issue was caused by NEI / CodeChicken adding a hidden §h tooltip marker to the first tooltip line.
HexText item names were rendering that hidden marker as a tiny visible tail at the end of the name.
The renderer now strips the hidden §h marker safely without breaking stack counts.
Trailing §r cleanup is still useful for lang entries, but §h was the real cause of the NEI hover tooltip artifact.
Result: styled item names, orb names, and hover tooltips now render cleanly with no extra smushed character at the end.

entries.title: Skills Balance and API Cleanup
entries.bannerTitle: Black Coffin and Dragon Fist tuning update
entries.summary: Recent skill work focused on Black Coffin PvP balance, Dragon Fist server stability, cleaner config pages, NBT unlock checks, and API documentation for scripting.
entries.actionSubtitle: PvP tuning is now mostly config-driven
details: Black Coffin damage tuning was moved further into server config so future PvP and PvE balance changes can be adjusted without rebuilding the mod.
Black Coffin now supports defense-aware PvP Body chip scaling, allowing target DBC Defense to reduce the guaranteed Body chip instead of ignoring defense entirely.
Black Coffin level checks were tightened: level 0 blocks charging and casting, level 1 allows normal only, level 2 allows chant, and level 3 unlocks the third-form modifier.
Black Coffin and Dragon Fist config options were reorganized under the unified Skills section, with shorter keys for cleaner config GUI display.
Legacy and duplicate config entries were cleaned up, including old Black Coffin, Dragon Fist, and build-height test options.
Dragon Fist server optimization was added to reduce lag from active Dragon Fist entities, including active-entity cleanup, tick throttling, and max lifetime safety checks.
Dragon Fist PvP damage was nerfed through config multipliers while keeping PvE damage mostly unchanged.
Custom PvP death messages were added for Dragon Fist and Black Coffin so player deaths no longer appear as unrelated mob kills.
Black Coffin PvP balance is now controlled mainly through bcPvpN, bcPvpC, bcPvpT, bcChipN, bcChipC, bcChipT, bcChipDefScale, and bcChipDefFloor.
Dragon Fist PvP balance is now controlled mainly through dfPvpN, dfPvpR, dfPvpL, dfPvpB, and dfPvpAll.
New API reference documents were prepared for HexMasterAPI, HexDragonFistAPI, and the broader HexColorText API index to make scripting support easier to maintain.
Memory cleanup and server diagnostic scripts were tested to help track script-side lag, item/entity buildup, and server memory usage during development.

Master GUI now supports colorful friendship and completion bars, rank-colored lesson stars, TEST badges, COMPLETE stamps, and cleaner overall completion display.
Cached master portraits now stay rendered after walking away from loaded NPCs, using remembered/cached render data instead of falling back to initials during normal gameplay.
